subject: Follow-up: Data handling & support access clarifications from today’s call
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@ledgerpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Data handling & support access clarifications from today’s call

Hi Olivia —

Great to meet you and Rajesh earlier. Thanks for walking through LedgerPay’s transaction flows; helpful context. Per our discussion I wanted to recap the data- and access-related items we agreed to clarify and the next steps so your security team can sign off on a pilot.

Quick recap (items you asked about):
- PII scope: cardholder name, email, billing addresses, and transaction metadata (no PAN stored with Redwood)
- Retention: you indicated a default window of 90 days for reference logs, with 7–30 day TTLs for derived metadata depending on your retention policy
- Logging/audit: need at least 1 year of immutable audit logs for support access events
- Data residency: production workload to remain in us-east-1, no cross-region backups without explicit approval
- Support access & RBAC: LedgerPay requires least-privilege separation, break-glass with explicit customer approval flow, and console-level fine-grained roles

Next steps I promised on the call:
1) Share a DPA + SOC2 point summary and our support break-glass process (we'll redact internal admin emails).
2) Confirm the ability to pin a model and data residency to us-east-1 for the pilot.
3) Draft a minimal RBAC mapping (roles + permissions) you can iterate on with Rajesh.

What I need from you (if possible by EOD Wed):
- Confirm the final retention windows you want Redwood to follow (e.g., transaction logs = 90 days, derived telemetry = 30 days)
- Any internal contacts for legal/compliance who should receive the DPA

Attachments: I’ll follow up with the DPA and a short break-glass playbook in a separate email (attaching redwood-dpa-draft.pdf and support-breakglass-playbook-v1.pdf).

If that alignment looks right, I’ll loop in Connor and Soojin to put together the RBAC mapping and an architecture diagram for the pilot.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---

From: Olivia Park <olivia@ledgerpay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Singh <rajesh.singh@ledgerpay.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & support access clarifications from today’s call

Karthik —

Thanks for the notes, that matches our discussion. A few clarifications from Rajesh's side:

- Confirmed: LedgerPay will not allow PANs to be stored in any third-party service. Any tokens must be one-way and reversible only by our vault.
- Retention: transaction logs = 90 days (audit copies retained for 1 year in read-only archival), derived telemetry = 30 days, and access logs = 13 months for compliance.
- Audit/logging detail: every support session must generate an immutable event with actor, timestamp, session-id, and exact resource path (e.g., /customers/{ledger_id}/events).
- Support access policy: break-glass is allowed only after a Jira ticket is opened and a named LedgerPay approver (rotating on-call) signs off via email; emergency phone approval acceptable but must be followed up with DRI sign-off within 24h.
- Residency: us-east-1 only for production; test/staging can be in other regions.

Rajesh asked if Redwood can provide a templated RBAC mapping (roles: read-only observer, support-analyst, escalation-admin) and a short runbook on how break-glass events are audited. Also, please attach the DPA.

We'll get you the legal/compliance contact (CC'ing our procurement soon).

Thanks,
Olivia
Head of Ops
LedgerPay

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 17:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: Data handling & support access clarifications from today’s call

Team —

Forwarding LedgerPay's clarifications. They’re firm on: no PAN storage, 90-day transaction logs (archival read-only 1yr), 13-month access log retention, and strict break-glass requiring Jira + approver sign-off. They want:
- Templated RBAC mapping (roles noted by Olivia)
- Break-glass runbook that captures immutable events (actor, timestamp, session-id, resource path) and an approval trail
- Confirmation that production can be pinned to us-east-1 and that we won’t create cross-region backups without their approval

Can each of you own the following so I can get back to LedgerPay by EOD tomorrow?
- Connor: draft the break-glass playbook PDF (include audit event schema + sample log entries). Mark it as "for customer review".
- Soojin: produce a one-page RBAC mapping (role -> minimal permissions) and confirm technical feasibility to enforce at the route/resource level.
- Marissa: confirm DPA + SOC2 summary and add any notes about our KMS/HSM controls (customer wants assurance around key separation).

I'll stitch these together with an architecture diagram (quick sketch attached: arch-diagram-ledgerpay-setup.png) and send to Olivia/Rajesh. If any of these are blocked by legal/infra approvals, flag immediately.

Thanks —
Karthik

Onward,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@ledgerpay.com>, Rajesh Singh <rajesh.singh@ledgerpay.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & support access clarifications from today’s call — artifacts attached

Hi Olivia / Rajesh —

Thanks again for the clear requirements. Attached are the initial artifacts we discussed: redwood-dpa-draft.pdf (DPA summary + standard language), support-breakglass-playbook-v1.pdf (what Connor drafted; includes event schema + sample audit entry), and a one-page RBAC mapping (Soojin's draft condensed into the attached PDF).

High-level answers to your must-haves:
- PANs: Redwood will not store PANs for LedgerPay; we support tokenization patterns where tokens are reversible only by your vault (we can add contractual language in the DPA).
- Retention: we will configure transaction logs = 90 days TTL, derived telemetry = 30 days TTL, and access/audit logs retained for 13 months in WORM-style archival.
- Data residency: pilot environment pinned to us-east-1; snapshots/backups will not be copied cross-region without explicit approval from LedgerPay.
- Break-glass: proposed flow: (1) open Jira ticket, (2) LedgerPay approver replies with explicit approval email, (3) Redwood enables temporary scoped support role for that session, (4) session recorded and immutable audit event written, (5) post-incident review within 24h. We included the audit event schema in the playbook.

Requested next steps / ask list:
- Olivia/Rajesh: confirm you’re okay with the three attached artifacts or provide redlines by Fri 2026-10-16.
- LedgerPay legal: please confirm preferred DPA contact (we’ll send a tracked DocuSign link once we have the approver).
- Redwood: Connor to update playbook with any LedgerPay redlines; Soojin to translate RBAC mapping into a concrete policy (IAM + route-level enforcement) and share expected ETA.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute working session this week to walk through the break-glass flow and sample audit entries. Connor and Soojin will join.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dpa-draft.pdf (DPA + SOC2 summary), support-breakglass-playbook-v1.pdf (audit schema + runbook), arch-diagram-ledgerpay-setup.png (pilot architecture sketch)
